pr_title: Improve Google Assistant cover assumed state handling
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
* Setup commandOnlyOpenClose for assumed state entities
* Revert special handling of state reporting
* Report empty state for assumed state entities


## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.

- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)

- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information
<!--
  Details are important, and help maintainers processing your PR.
  Please be sure to fill out additional details, if applicable.
-->

Google will issue queries for covers even if they are marked as commandOnlyOpenClose when the device is opened up in a google home/nest display device. When we error here, we will report a query response with an offline device.

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #43178
- This PR reverts changes from #23498

pr_comments: @balloob i reverted your change for opportunistic covers here. I don't think it's needed now that we report it as command only. Do you have any recollection of why it was added instead of commandOnly. My guess is command only didn't exist back then.

I don't think this would reintroduce https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/23226 , but i don't entirely follow why it was done this way.

We could potentially report commandOnly for the case of unknown state. But i think that would be wrong. Assumed state should be set if we can't find out state.

I may have to remove the revert of state override. This seem to indicate a need to report the state of the command even though it is unknown. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60147925/how-to-respond-to-a-query-intent-for-devices-with-a-genuinely-unknown-state-wil

## The problem
I manage my covers from ha-tahoma (https://github.com/iMicknl/ha-tahoma). Inside Home Assistant everything is working properly. I have no problem of integration between Home Assistant and ha-tahoma.

I connected my Home Assistant setup with my Google Assistant to manage Covers.
I can properly import my Home Assistant devices. I have the covers properly imported in GHA (Google Home Application).
However my devices are reported as "Offline". I can successfully open the covers but I have systematically this errors in my logs

I tried to force assumed_state to false but behavior didn't changed.

Screenshots
https://photos.app.goo.gl/gNW4KzkDGKpPwPGB6 in GHA

## Environment
I have installed Homeassistant 0.117.6
I'm running Ubuntu 20.04

My configuration
- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.6
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core):  Ubuntu using https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/installation/raspberry-pi/
- Integration causing this issue: Google Assistant
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```yaml
tts:
  - platform: google_translate

group: !include groups.yaml
automation: !include automations.yaml
script: !include scripts.yaml
scene: !include scenes.yaml
http:
  ssl_certificate: REDACTED
  ssl_key: REDACTED
google_assistant:
  project_id: REDACTED
  report_state: true
  service_account: !include ha.json
homeassistant:
  customize_domain:
    cover:
      assumed_state: false
```
